key_insight: WFDroneBench shows that risk-aware sensor and drone deployment can substantially improve early wildfire detection, especially when the underlying fire-risk maps are accurate.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark provides a reproducible way to compare deployment and routing strategies for real-world wildfire monitoring systems that combine ML risk prediction with optimization.
method: Open-source Python benchmark integrating risk maps with optimization-based placement/routing
Tests sensor, charging-station, and drone strategies under realistic wildfire spread simulations
Compares 2 ground-detector and 3 drone-routing strategies across standardized metrics
evidence_signal: The benchmark spans 7,746 scenarios across 49 locations using historical ignitions, real-world risk maps, and simulated fire spread, and the risk-aware Max-Coverage strategy achieved the fastest detection on the hardest fires when maps were sufficiently accurate.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on risk-map quality, so deployment gains may weaken if the predicted ignition patterns are inaccurate or outdated.
paper_title: WFDroneBench: A Benchmark for Sensor Placement and Drone Routing for Wildfire Detection
